evidence.intree_statement: Lemma monic_iff_kernel_pzero {x y : C} (f : x ~> y) : Monic f ↔ (∀ (z : C) (u : z ~> x), f ∘ u ≈ zero_mor → u ≈ zero_mor).
Class Monic {x y} (f : x ~> y) := { monic : ∀ z (g1 g2 : z ~> x), f ∘ g1 ≈ f ∘ g2 → g1 ≈ g2 }.
Lemma epic_iff_cokernel_pzero {x y : C} (f : x ~> y) : Epic f ↔ (∀ (z : C) (u : y ~> z), u ∘ f ≈ zero_mor → u ≈ zero_mor).

statement_record.book: Theorem 3 lists six elementary rules for chasing diagrams with MEMBERS of objects in any abelian category: (i) f monic iff ∀ x ∈_m a, fx ≡ 0 ⟹ x ≡ 0; (ii) f monic iff ∀ x,x' ∈_m a, fx ≡ fx' ⟹ x ≡ x'; (iii) g epi iff every z ∈_m c has y ∈_m b with gy ≡ z; (iv) h = 0 iff hx ≡ 0 ∀ x; (v) a→b→c exact at b iff gf = 0 and every y with gy ≡ 0 has x with fx ≡ y; (vi) subtraction rule. These presuppose the member apparatus (def-member): members = arrows into a, the equivalence x ≡ y iff ∃ epis u,v with xu = yv, a zero member, and negatives.
statement_record.intree: Monic f is DEFINED as left cancellation ∀ g1 g2, f∘g1 ≈ f∘g2 → g1 ≈ g2 (Theory/Morphisms.v, = rule (ii) read with strict ≈ in place of ≡). Structure/Abelian.v proves the abelian-category vanishing tests monic_iff_kernel_pzero (Monic f ↔ ∀u, f∘u ≈ 0 → u ≈ 0, = rule (i) read with ≈ for ≡, since in an abelian category x ≡ 0 ⟺ x ≈ 0) and epic_iff_cokernel_pzero (a co-vanishing test u∘f ≈ 0 → u ≈ 0).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the MEMBER calculus that IS the substance of Theorem 3 is entirely absent — no notion of member (x ∈_m a), no equivalence ≡, no member-classes, zero member, or negatives, and no `member' file/definition anywhere in the tree. Only the categorical shadows of rules (i) [monic_iff_kernel_pzero] and (ii) [the definition of Monic] are present, stated over ALL morphisms with strict ≈ rather than over member-classes with ≡. Rule (iii) (epi = surjective-on-members) has NO in-tree counterpart — epic_iff_cokernel_pzero is a co-vanishing test, a DIFFERENT statement, not the surjectivity characterization. Rules (iv), (v) (member-exactness, which also needs the absent `exact at' predicate), and (vi) (subtraction) are absent.
